text:
alex: Heads-up — hit a weird UX gotcha in the Go SDK generator while onboarding a sample app. iterator.Next() can end up blocking even after ctx.Cancel when an auth refresh happens mid-stream.

ciara: ugh that sounds bad. repro?

alex: minimal repro: start a streaming generate with a short ctx timeout, force token refresh by rotating creds, and Next() never returns even though ctx is Done().

sam: can you paste the snippet?

alex: sure 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 300*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
iter, _ := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
for iter.Next() {
  // process
}
if err := iter.Err(); err != nil {
  fmt.Println("iter error:", err)
}
```
The problem is the internal handshake goroutine blocks on the auth refresh HTTP call and doesn't select on ctx.Done(), so Next()'s channel read never unblocks.

lee: timeline: this happens when the SDK does a mid-stream auth refresh and the refresh call hangs, right? not a server-side stall on tokens?

alex: exactly. server responds fine but the SDK HTTP client used for refresh isn't honoring the request ctx in that goroutine. Also we don't expose a Close/Stop API on the iterator to proactively tear down the handshake.

jordan: interesting. is this only with the sampleapp token refresh flow or could customers hit this in Dedicated/Private?

alex: could be any long-lived stream with expiring creds — e.g., customers using short-lived STS tokens or rotating secrets. So it has real production impact.

ciara: quick mitigation for sample app: wrap the token refresh transport to use req = req.WithContext(parentCtx) and add deadline checks. can we push a tiny patch to DevX sampleapp and an SDK hotfix?

sam: agree — two-prong: (1) sampleapp: show explicit Close/Cancel pattern in examples. (2) runtime: make refresh call select on ctx.Done() and set net/http timeout. Also expose iterator.Close() that closes internal chans.

lee: API proposal: add UninterruptibleStream bool? hate that. better: Iterator.Close() and ensure internal goroutines use a child ctx derived from the iterator's ctx that we cancel on Close. That keeps signature stable.

jordan: sounds reasonable. can we add a small unit test that simulates a blocked refresh and ensures Next() returns after Close or ctx cancel?

alex: yeah I wrote a flaky test that reproduces reliably by making the refresh handler sleep 5s while client ctx times out at 100ms. I can push a draft PR to devex and link it.

ciara: please include a concise reproduction in the sampleapp docs and call out "use Close() in long-lived services or rotate tokens carefully".

sam: assigned — alex will open PRs: one to go-sdk to add Close() + ctx-aware refresh, one to sampleapp with docs + example. Leave a TODO for a compatibility note in CHANGELOG.

bot-deploy: deploy job queued for branch alex/stream-iter-close-fix — build started. :rocket:

alex: will post the PR links here once ready, thanks all for quick triage.

lee: follow-up: also consider adding a lint in sampleapp that highlights when people use global contexts for streams. small DX win.

alex: good call. I'll add a comment in the sampleapp PR about ctx patterns and include a short snippet showing 'context.WithCancel' usage to gracefully stop streams.

ciara: great — thanks. keep it small and focused, we want this in a patch release if possible.
